title: PRAIM: radiologists using Vara MG in the German mammography screening program detect 17.6% more breast cancers without more recalls
summary: Across 463,094 women at 12 German screening sites, radiologists who used Vara MG found 6.7 cancers per 1,000 against 5.7 without it, with no rise in recalls.
account: The PRAIM study followed routine mammography screening of women aged 50 to 69 at 12 sites of the German screening program from July 2021 to February 2023. Radiologists chose for each examination whether to read it in the Vara MG viewer, a CE-certified product from the Berlin company Vara. The software tagged examinations that it judged normal and raised a safety-net alert on examinations that it judged suspicious. Of 463,094 women, 260,739 were read with AI support. Radiologists who used the AI found 6.7 cancers per 1,000 women against 5.7 per 1,000 without it, a 17.6% higher rate. The recall rate was 37.4 per 1,000 with AI and 38.3 per 1,000 without. The safety net led to 204 cancer diagnoses that the authors judge would otherwise have been missed. The study was observational, so radiologists chose when to use the AI, and the authors report a reading-behavior bias. Vara funded the study, took part in its design and writing, and employed three of the authors.
purpose: Vara MG was built to display mammograms and to preclassify screening examinations as normal or suspicious for radiologists. The higher detection rate was that purpose.
deployer: Radiologists at 12 screening units of the German mammography screening program
